AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To explore whether the physical activity (PA) component of the Coordinated Approach to Child Health Early Childhood (CATCH EC) program helps increasing preschoolers' PA during active times at preschool.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Head Start centers in Houston, Texas, 2009 to 2010 school year.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 439 preschoolers aged 3 to 5 years (3 intervention centers, n = 220; 3 comparison centers, n = 219).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: The CATCH EC preschool-based teacher-led nutrition and PA program.

AbstractText.Label: MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Preschoolers' PA was measured at baseline and postintervention using the System for Observing Fitness Instruction Time-Preschool version, a direct observation method measuring PA at the classroom level. Parent surveys provided demographic data.

AbstractText.Label: ANALYSIS
AbstractText.content: Pre-to-post changes in preschoolers' PA were examined using the Mann-Whitney U test.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Results show a significant decrease in the percentage time preschoolers spent in level 2 PA (low activity) at intervention ( P = .005) and comparison ( P = .041) centers. Indoor vigorous activity increased significantly on an average by +6.04% pre-to-post intervention among preschoolers in the intervention group ( P = .049); no significant change was found in the comparison group.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The CATCH EC favorably increased indoor vigorous PA level among low-income children attending Head Start.
